name: Project Checklist
description: A simple end-to-end task list to plan, run and finish any project with confidence.

items.text: Write a one-sentence statement of the project goal
List the key deliverables the project must produce
Set what is in scope and clearly note what is out
items.note: A short out-of-scope list prevents creep later.

items.text: Name the project sponsor and the main point of contact
Agree on how you will measure success
Break the project into clear, manageable tasks
Put the tasks in a logical order and note dependencies
Estimate the time each task will take
Set a realistic start and finish date for each task
Identify any tools, materials, or budget you will need
Give every task a single accountable owner
Confirm each person has the time and access to deliver
Book any rooms, tools, or services in advance
Share the plan so the whole team knows their part
items.note: One shared document avoids version confusion.

items.text: Set a regular check-in time to review progress
Start the highest-priority tasks first
Update task status as work is completed
Flag blockers early and decide who will clear them
Track time and spending against the plan
Keep stakeholders informed with a short status update
items.note: A weekly one-paragraph update is usually enough.

items.text: Compare actual progress against the original timeline
Re-prioritize tasks if deadlines or scope change
Confirm quality before marking any deliverable done
Document any changes and tell the people affected
Adjust the budget or schedule if estimates were off
Confirm every deliverable is complete and approved
Get final sign-off from the sponsor or client
Hand over files, access, and documentation
Note what went well and what to improve next time
items.note: A short lessons-learned list saves the next project.

items.text: Thank the team and formally close the project

faq.a: It is an ordered list of the tasks needed to plan, run, and finish a project. It keeps goals, owners, deadlines, and deliverables in one place so the work stays on track.

faq.q: How do I create a project checklist?
faq.a: Start with the goal, break the work into clear tasks, assign an owner and due date to each, then group them by stage. Review and update the list as the project moves forward.

faq.q: Who should use this project checklist?
faq.a: Anyone leading work with multiple steps or people: team leads, managers, freelancers, students, and volunteers. It scales from a small personal project to a cross-team effort.

faq.q: How is a project checklist different from a project plan?
faq.a: A plan describes timelines, budgets, and strategy in detail; a checklist turns that plan into bite-sized tasks you can tick off. Use the checklist to make sure the plan actually gets done.

faq.q: Can I print this project checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Download the printable PDF, share it with your team, and check off each task as the project moves from kickoff to final review.
